subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acme-retail.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@shopquick.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side so we’re aligned and have clear next steps. I’ve kept this focused on the pain, goals, and the structured-output requirements we discussed.

Pain points you shared
- Search & product detail generation are inconsistent across categories; content teams spend manual effort reformatting outputs.
- Current pipeline (in-house LLM + rule post-processing) fails on edge SKUs and causes downstream QA workload.
- Loss of deterministic outputs when calls involve external tool data (pricing, inventory).

Goals / success criteria
- Deterministic structured outputs for downstream systems (JSON schema validated) >= 95% of production queries.
- Support tool/function-calling so agent workflows can fetch canonical product metadata (pricing, inventory, imagery) and merge into the final JSON.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for typical 1-2-turn generation + tool calls.
- Error handling: explicit "fallback_reason" field when tool call is unavailable.

Current stack (from today’s call)
- In-house LLM model (served via internal endpoints) for copy & metadata enrichment
- Post-processing pipeline (Python) that validates+normalizes output into your product JSON
- Tools: internal pricing API, inventory service, and a 3rd-party image CDN

Structured-output and tool-calling specifics we discussed
- You need a single deterministic JSON schema that downstream services can parse without heuristics.
- The LLM should call the pricing & inventory tools via function/tool-calling (agent workflow) and populate final fields.
- If a tool call fails, the model should still produce a valid JSON with a standardized error field and minimal fallback values.

Attached: short recap PDF + a draft JSON schema example (draft-json-schema-v1.json). Please review the schema and flag any missing product attributes.

Next steps (I’ll do)
1) Share the draft JSON schema (attached) and an example agent workflow.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering team next week to map tool endpoints and auth.
3) Provide a pilot plan with metrics & timeline (we’ll include deterministic formatting tests).

Would Tuesday 7/21 10am PT work for a 60-min tech session?

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks Jordan — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Determinism: when you say ">= 95% of production queries", we’re thinking of a phased rollout: pilot on Home & Kitchen category first, then expand. 95% is a good target for pilot acceptance.
2) Tool auth: our pricing API uses token-based auth; the inventory service requires a client cert. We’ll need Redwood to support integrating both for the tech session.
3) Fallback behavior: we prefer explicit nulls with a "fallback_reason" string rather than placeholder text.

We can do Tue 7/21 10am PT — I’ll invite our lead backend engineer, Priya.

Alex

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the confirmations. I’ve attached a draft JSON schema (draft-json-schema-v1.json) and included an inline example of the minimal expected output format below. This is intentionally strict to make deterministic parsing straightforward.

Example expected output (minimal):
{
  "product_id": "string (SKU)",
  "title": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "price": { "amount": "number", "currency": "string" },
  "inventory": { "available": "integer", "location": "string" },
  "images": ["string (url)"],
  "fallback_reason": "string | null",
  "metadata": { "source": "string", "confidence": "number" }
}

Agent workflow (high-level):
1) Prompt to LLM: produce the JSON output and call the PricingTool and InventoryTool when needed.
2) LLM issues function calls: PricingTool.getPrice(sku) and InventoryTool.getAvailability(sku, region).
3) System collects tool responses; the model composes the final JSON and returns it.
4) Validation layer checks schema; if validation fails, return a structured error payload with "fallback_reason" and the invalid fields.

Deterministic formatting success criteria (proposed):
- 99% of pilot responses exactly match the schema structure (same keys and types).
- 95% of non-null numeric fields within 5% of canonical pricing when a tool call succeeds.
- Structured fallback used for all tool failures (no free-text substitutions).

Please let us know any missing attributes and confirm Tue 7/21 10am PT for the deep-dive. I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda (auth, endpoints, certs, pilot scope).

Jordan

Success metrics we’ll share in the pilot dashboard:
- Schema pass rate (goal >= 99%)
- Tool call success rate (goal >= 99% for pricing & inventory)
- p95 end-to-end latency (goal < 400ms)
- % queries with fallback_reason populated (goal < 3%)
